knowledge:
- key_parameters: countData=The filtered and normalized expression matrix (e.g., voom-transformed expression values) with genes in rows and cells in columns ;; condition=A vector of cell-annotation/condition groupings for the single cells ;; numCores=The number of cores to be used for parallel processing based on hardware specifications
- alternatives: The documentation notes that users are free to use alternative preprocessing strategies with different filtering/normalization methods instead of the demonstrated edgeR/limma pipeline.
- when_to_use: Use when performing differential expression analysis on single-cell RNA-Seq (scRNA-Seq) data, particularly when a noise-tolerant, rank-based modeling approach is desired to compare two contrasting groups of cells.
- pitfalls: The input to the ROSeq function must be a filtered and normalized read count matrix (specifically, the documentation uses voom-transformed expression values, i.e., countData=samples$count$E). Passing raw, unfiltered, or unnormalized counts directly to ROSeq without proper preprocessing may lead to incorrect results.

workflows.name: roseq_de_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform rank-based differential expression analysis on single-cell RNA-Seq data.
input: count_matrix.csv (raw read count matrix with genes in rows and cells in columns)
cell_metadata.csv (cell-annotation/condition mapping cells to contrasting groups)
workflows.stages: 1. Load required libraries ;; 2. Filter cells and genes based on expression thresholds ;; 3. Perform TMM normalization using ROSeq::TMMnormalization ;; 4. Apply voom transformation using limma::voom ;; 5. Run differential expression analysis using ROSeq
workflows.code:
library(ROSeq)
library(edgeR)
library(limma)
samples<-list()
samples$count<-ROSeq::L_Tung_single$NA19098_NA19101_count
samples$group<-ROSeq::L_Tung_single$NA19098_NA19101_group
gene_names<-rownames(samples$count)
samples$count<-apply(samples$count,2,function(x) as.numeric(x))
rownames(samples$count)<-gene_names
samples$count<-samples$count[,colSums(samples$count> 0) > 2000]
gkeep<-apply(samples$count,1,function(x) sum(x>2)>=3)
samples$count<-samples$count[gkeep,]
samples$count<-limma::voom(ROSeq::TMMnormalization(samples$count))
output<-ROSeq(countData=samples$count$E, condition = samples$group, numCores=1)
